title: Fun YouTube Podcast: reframed 1080p sizzle cut and a branded graphics kit (lower-third + end-screen + vector logo)
grounding_note: VERBATIM from the Freelancer.com brief: raw YouTube podcast footage to be shaped into an engaging episode; "trim unwanted pauses or stumbles", "add clean transitions", "weave in light-hearted graphics or effects that match a casual, fun vibe", incorporate the client's existing logo "in the intro, a lower-third, or the end screen" so branding feels consistent "without overpowering the content"; deliverables = a fully edited 1080p (or higher) video, the editing project file, and "any custom graphic assets you create, delivered separately in PNG/transparent or vector format". REASONABLY ENRICHED to make it a runnable Adobe-connector benchmark: (1) the editing project file is delivered as the connector's own packaged artifacts (reframed 1080p master + sizzle reel + asset kit), since the connector has no Premiere/FCP/Resolve project export — this is stated plainly to the client as the equivalent hand-off; (2) "trim pauses/stumbles" is honestly realized as an AI visual-engagement Quick Cut sizzle/highlight pass (video_create_quick_cut is engagement-based, NOT timestamp trimming) PLUS a full-length reframed master — the spec is explicit that frame-accurate stumble removal is the one human-finishable step; (3) the "custom graphic assets" PNG-transparent/vector deliverables (cleaned + vectorized logo, lower-third plate, end-screen plate) are produced through the headless image_*/vectorize chain. No capability is invented: no generative fill, no compositing of the graphics INTO the video (delivered "separately" exactly as the brief requests), no text-to-image, no upscaling.
one_line_ask: Turn the raw podcast footage into a reframed 1080p YouTube master plus a cold-open sizzle and a fun branded graphics kit (vector logo + lower-third + end-screen as PNG-transparent/vector), delivered separately.
full_brief:
You are editing one episode of a casual, fun YouTube podcast. The client supplies the raw multi-cam-ish recording (a single 1080p+ master with two speakers), their existing brand logo lockup (a flat PNG on a busy background), and a hand-shot lower-third texture plate. They want three things delivered: (A) a fully edited 1080p YouTube-ready video that flows smoothly; (B) the working hand-off so they can tweak later; and (C) any custom graphic assets you create, delivered SEPARATELY in PNG/transparent or vector format, with their logo worked in tastefully in the intro / lower-third / end screen without overpowering the content.

Concretely: produce a punchy highlight/sizzle cut from the raw footage for the cold-open, and reframe the full episode to a clean 1080p YouTube frame. For the graphics kit: lift the client's logo off its busy background to a clean transparent PNG, color-correct and brand-tint it, then vectorize it to an infinitely-scalable SVG for the end screen. Build a lower-third "name plate" from the supplied texture plate: knock out the background, fill a clean solid brand-colored bar, tint it to match, crop it to a broadcast lower-third strip. License one subtle on-brand background texture from stock for the end-screen card. The vibe is light-hearted and casual — clean and consistent branding, never stiff or corporate.

'TRAILGREMLIN POD' is an invented, IP-clean mark.

chaining_note: Strict output->input chain. Steps 1-2 ingest all five supplied video clips (podcast_raw_master_1080p.mp4 + raw_supplemental_02/03/04/05.mp4, ~45s of total footage) into CC storage as ingested_video_assets. That set fans into the video branch: video_create_quick_cut (3) draws across all five clips for the ~12s engagement-based cold-open sizzle, while video_resize (4) reframes the full-length master specifically to a clean 1920x1080 YouTube frame (same length, no trim). The graphics kit is its own deep chain: logo background-removal (5) -> auto_tone (6) -> color_overlay = brand_logo_clean.png (7) -> vectorize = brand_logo_vector.svg (8). The texture-plate chain: auto_straighten (9) -> select_subject (10) -> invert_selection (11) -> fill_area solid bar (12) -> monochromatic_tint (13) -> crop_and_resize = lower_third_plate.png (14). Finally asset_license_and_download_stock (15) searches, licenses and downloads one subtle on-brand end-screen texture keyed to the cleaned brand logo (7). Every non-load step sets inputs_from to a prior step's named output; the deliverables (cold-open sizzle, reframed master, clean logo, vector logo, lower-third plate, end-screen texture) emerge directly from the chain.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship: 15 connector calls, 15 distinct Adobe tools, spanning three connector groups (asset/storage, video [A], photo/raster [C]). It is hard because the agent must HONESTLY decompose a Premiere/FCP/Resolve brief that has no direct connector analog: recognize that 'trim pauses/stumbles' cannot be done frame-accurately and instead deliver an engagement-based Quick Cut + a same-length reframed master (and flag the human-finishable trim), and that the 'custom graphic assets… delivered separately' are produced via the headless image_*/vectorize chain rather than composited into the video (which the connector cannot do and the brief does not ask for). It mixes async-widget [A] media steps with a deep headless [C] raster→vector pipeline, requires a correct select→invert→solid-fill→tint→crop sequence for the lower-third, and reuses the ingested video asset set across the two media branches. No not-available capability is used (no gen-fill, no compositing, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no timestamp trim, no per-artboard export). The only non-headless steps are the two [A] media calls (Quick Cut + video_resize), which are explicitly in scope for the Adobe×Claude product.

reverify.banned_capability_check: No banned capabilities present. All 15 steps use real Adobe connector actions: asset upload (init/finalize), video_create_quick_cut [A] engagement-highlight (not timestamp trim), video_resize [A] same-length reframe, and a headless raster/vector chain (remove_background, auto_tone, color_overlay, vectorize, auto_straighten, select_subject, invert_selection, image_fill_area=solid-color fill within canvas, monochromatic_tint, crop_and_resize to lower-third strip, license_and_download_stock). No generative expand/outpaint, no upscale/super-resolution, no text-to-image, no from-scratch art/logo, no object-removal-with-reconstruction, no compositing graphics into the video, no image_apply_lens_blur mask. image_fill_area is used only as a solid-color fill of an inverted in-canvas region and crop_and_resize only crops down, so no canvas growth. Gen-free.
reverify.notes: IP/naming: the client brand was renamed to the invented, non-colliding mark 'TRAILGREMLIN POD'; the name string appears only in brand_logo_lockup.png's gen_prompt, all other fields reference the brand generically. INPUTS completeness: all five supplied video clips (podcast_raw_master_1080p.mp4 + raw_supplemental_02/03/04/05.mp4) are now ingested in steps 1-2 and drawn on by the Quick Cut cold-open (step 3), giving ~45s of real footage behind the ~12s sizzle; the master is reframed full-length by video_resize (step 4). The lower_third_texture_plate.jpg feeds the plate chain (steps 9-14) and brand_logo_lockup.png feeds the graphics-kit chain (steps 5-8). DESCOPE: the episode content-summary deliverable was removed — the source video has no audio stream and no media_summarize step remained to produce it — and the end-screen stock license (step 15) is now keyed to the cleaned brand logo instead of the removed summary. The task remains real, coherent, and fully connector-doable.
